newsitem.title: BELGIUM: NATO ministers back new Bosnia force.
newsitem.headline: NATO ministers back new Bosnia force.

text.p: NATO foreign ministers on Tuesday formally approved a plan to send between 25,000 and 30,000 troops to monitor the peace accords in Bosnia next year, diplomats said.
The 16 ministers agreed that a Stabilisation Force (SFOR) should replace the current alliance-led Implementation Force (IFOR) when its mandate expires on December 20.

The new force, which will be endorsed by a U.N. Security Council resolution next week, will remain in Bosnia for 18 months with reviews every six months and be progressively reduced as the mission's expiry date approaches.

"From now on, the destiny of the Bosnians will be more and more in their own hands," French Foreign Minister Herve de Charette said in his opening speech to a two-day meeting of NATO foreign ministers.
Some 17 non-NATO countries, including Russia, which are taking part in the IFOR mission, despatched to oversee implementation of last year's Dayton peace accords, have agreed to participate in SFOR.
NATO hopes the cooperation will help it build better relations with former enemies it will not invite to join the alliance at a special summit in July next year.
